info.title: بذور الأمل Platform API
info.description: Generated from the implementation. The SRS TD-3 route registry is the canonical contract (§3.1); this document must conform to it and is never hand-edited.

get.description: Redirects to Google with state + PKCE (§4.1b steps 1–2, TD-12).

§4.1b routing: existing identity → session by status; pre-provisioned email match → bind identity → session by status; unknown → onboarding. Failures are REDIRECTS to /login?error=<key>, never the TD-3.8 envelope (§4.1b step 7).

302.description: Redirect by routing decision, or to /login?error=<key> on failure.

post.description: The ONLY cookie-authenticated route (TD-12). Requires X-Requested-With and an Origin matching PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Rotation, the 10s predecessor grace window, and reuse detection are per TD-4.13 and §18 T1–T12.

200.description: New access token; a rotated refresh cookie unless the grace window applied.

401.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). All refusal reasons are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.summary: Log out of the current session
post.description: Revokes the current session only; other devices are unaffected (TD-4.14).

get.description: Identity, roles, branch scopes, account_status and approved child links. The only endpoint (with logout) that a Pending session may call (TD-1).

post.description: Public, gated by the signed onboarding token in X-Onboarding-Token (§4.1b step 4c). Adult self-registration or parent+child in ONE transaction (TD-4.1). Identity comes solely from the token payload — the schema rejects email/provider_subject_id outright (§20 rule 9). New accounts enter Pending.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT on token replay; DUPLICATE if the identity exists.

503.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). consent text version not configured (§2.3).

get.description: Admin or Super Admin only (TD-2), re-asserted against live rows per request because approvals are a TD-12 high-risk surface. Two item types share the queue: `registration` (a pending applicant together with any pending child and link that arrived as one §4.1 bundle) and `family-link` (a standalone §4.3 "Link a Child" request). A pending child is never listed separately — it appears inside its parent's bundle so the family is approved once. Paginated per TD-10 (default 25, max 100), oldest first.

200.description: Queue page; each item carries its applicants and what approving it will change.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN when the caller is no longer Active or the admin role assignment no longer exists (TD-12).

post.description: TD-4.2: parent activation, child activation, link approval and the audit row commit in ONE transaction — §4.3 requires all three atomically, since a half-approved bundle is a parent who can see a child whose own record is still Pending. TD-1 transition Pending → Active. Approval does NOT assign roles. Concurrent decisions are first-wins (TD-15.3): the loser gets 409, never a 500.

200.description: Approved; reports the item type and how many accounts were activated.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN (TD-12 freshness or TD-2 role).

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT when the item was already decided.

post.description: Requires a reason (§5.6, §14.2) of at most 500 characters (TD-9) — rejecting a family's application without recording why is not an auditable decision. Rejection is atomic across the bundle in the same way as approval (TD-4.2): the parent and child are never left half-decided. TD-1 transition Pending → Rejected.

200.description: Rejected; the reason is stored on the decision and in the audit row.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED when the reason is missing or too long.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT when the item was already decided.

delete.description: Admin or Super Admin (TD-2), asserted against live rows per request. §4.3 Revision 16: soft-deleting the row IS the revocation mechanism — TD-1 keeps `Approved` terminal and no `Approved → Revoked` transition exists, because enforcement is already complete: the `X-Active-Child-ID` middleware re-checks the link on every request, so revocation takes effect on the very NEXT request. Follows the ordinary TD-4.8 soft-delete transaction (`deleted_at`/`deleted_by` + Trash snapshot + `familylink.revoke` audit carrying both parties and the reason). A reason of 1–500 characters is required (TD-9). The TD-6 partial unique index covers non-deleted rows only, so the same pair can be requested again later as a fresh Pending link.

200.description: Revoked; the parent loses access to that child immediately.

400.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). VALIDATION_FAILED when the reason is missing or too long.

403.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). FORBIDDEN (TD-12 freshness or TD-2 role).

404.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). NOT_FOUND for an unknown or already-revoked link.

409.description: Error envelope (TD-3.8). STATE_CONFLICT when the link is not Approved — pending and rejected links are decided through the approval queue.

get.description: Ordered by display_order ASC NULLS LAST then name (ar-x-icu collated, §2.2/TD-10). Admins see their scoped branches; Super Admins see all.

post.description: Admin or Super Admin (TD-2). display_order is Super Admin only (§2.2).

patch.description: Optimistic locking on `version` (TD-15): a stale version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT rather than overwriting silently.

delete.description: Prohibited while Rooms or Groups reference it (TD-5) — 409 STATE_CONFLICT. Writes a Trash snapshot and an audit row (TD-4.8).

get.description: Public. Checks database, storage and job-queue components (TD-14); §19.1 step 8 asserts a 200 here on deployment.

503.description: At least one component is down.
